'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Afghan peace process]]
***[[United States Army]] [[General (United States)|General]] [[Austin S. Miller]] announces that [[United States Armed Forces|U.S. troops]] have started their [[2021 withdrawal of U.S. troops from Afghanistan|withdrawal]] from [[Afghanistan]]. However, he also warned that Afghan security forces "must be ready" to take over. [https://www.stripes.com/news/middle-east/us-general-afghanistan-security-forces-must-be-ready-to-take-over-1.671148 (''Stars and Stripes'')]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[93rd Academy Awards]]
**''[[Nomadland (film)|Nomadland]]'' wins [[Academy Award for Best Picture|Best Picture]] at this year's [[Academy Awards]]. ''Nomadland'' director [[Chloé Zhao]] wins [[Academy Award for Best Director|Best Director]], the second woman to win this award. [https://www.theguardian.com/film/2021/apr/26/nomadland-wins-best-picture-oscar-chloe-zhao (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Anthony Hopkins]] becomes [[List of oldest and youngest Academy Award winners and nominees|the oldest person]] to win [[Academy Award for Best Actor|Best Actor]] for his role in ''[[The Father (2020 film)|The Father]]'' at 83. [https://www.theguardian.com/film/2021/apr/26/anthony-hopkins-is-oldest-ever-oscar-winner-after-taking-best-actor-for-the-father (''The Guardian'')]
**[[South Korea|South Korean]] actress [[Youn Yuh-jung]] wins [[Academy Award for Best Supporting Actress|Best Supporting Actress]] for ''[[Minari (film)|Minari]]'', becoming the first [[Koreans|Korean]] to win in any of the acting categories. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20210426000427 (''The Korean Herald'')]

'''Businesses and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]
**The [[Italy|Italian]] [[Government of Italy|government]] signs a large package of investment and reforms that will be financed by the [[European Union]]’s [[Euro|€]]800 billion recovery fund, of which the country received €191.5 billion including €69 billion of grants. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-25/italy-signs-off-on-investment-reform-package-to-deploy-eu-funds (Bloomberg News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[KRI Nanggala (402)|KRI ''Nanggala'' (402)]]
**[[Indonesia]]n authorities say that the [[KRI Nanggala (402)|navy submarine]] that sunk off the coast of [[Bali]] was found split into three parts in the ocean. It comes after officials received signals from a location of {{cvt|838|m}}. The authorities also say that the 53 crew members are confirmed dead. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/indonesia-finds-debris-from-missing-submarine-says-it-sank-11619263840 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*[[Baghdad hospital fire]]
**[[Prime Minister of Iraq|Iraqi Prime Minister]] [[Mustafa Al-Kadhimi]] suspends his [[Minister of Health (Iraq)|health minister]] and the [[Baghdad Governorate|Governor of Baghdad]], who will both be probed on the fire. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/middle-east/iraq-premier-suspends-health-minister-baghdad-governor/2220317 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Incidents at European amusement parks]]
**Riders are forced to climb down the top of the lift hill on the [[The Big One (roller coaster)|Big One]] [[roller coaster]] at the [[Blackpool Pleasure Beach]] after it broke down. [https://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/news/people-forced-to-climb-down-blackpools-iconic-rollercoaster-after-it-breaks-down-3213399 (''Blackpool Gazette'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi]], [[COVID-19 lockdown in India]]
*****[[Delhi]] extends its lockdown until May 3 amid a record breaking increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/delhi-lockdown-extended-by-a-week-says-chief-minister-arvind-kejriwal-2421403 (NDTV)]
****[[India]] reports 349,691 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is a world record for the fourth consecutive day, thereby bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 16.9 million. The country also reports a record 2,767 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|deaths]] in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 192,311. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/25/asia/india-covid-fourth-day-record-infections-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] surpasses 300,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://thehimalayantimes.com/nepal/covid-19-cases-soar-in-nepal-2000-infections-detected-after-nov-2020 (''The Himalayan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 11 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 140. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2105195/11-covid-deaths-2-438-new-cases-sunday (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Greece]] reports its first two cases of the Lineage B.1.617 variant first detected in [[India]]. [https://greekreporter.com/2021/04/25/indian-variant-of-coronavirus-arrives-in-greece/ (Greek Reporter)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Italy]] bans anyone who had travelled to [[India]] within the past 14 days from entering the country in order to reduce the spread of the [[Lineage B.1.617]] variant. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/india/550182-italy-bans-travel-from-india-amid-surge-in-variants (''The Hill'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Egypt]]
***[[Egypt]]ian [[President of Egypt|President]] [[Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] receives his first dose of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/egypts-sisi-receives-coronavirus-vaccine-2021-04-25/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***The [[Fiji]]an [[Ministry of Health (Fiji)|Health Ministry]] announces the introduction of containment zones in [[Lami, Fiji|Lami]], [[Suva]], and [[Nausori]] beginning tomorrow at 4:00 a.m. for 14 days after four community cases were detected. [https://www.fijitimes.com/covid-19-four-new-community-cases-lami-suva-and-nausori-to-go-into-lock-down-tomorrow-morning/ (''Fiji Times'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[India–United States relations]], [[Deployment of COVID-19 vaccines]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
**[[National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases|NIAID]] director [[Anthony Fauci]] says that the [[United States]] will consider sending unused [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccines]] and medical aid to [[India]] to help them combat their COVID-19 outbreak. [https://www.newindianexpress.com/world/2021/apr/25/biden-administrations-top-medical-adviser-fauci-says-us-considering-virus-aid-to-india-2294743.html (''The New Indian Express'')] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-04-25/u-s-to-consider-sending-india-unused-vaccine-doses-fauci-says (Bloomberg News)]
**[[National Security Advisor (United States)|U.S. National Security Advisor]] [[Jake Sullivan]] announces that the country will send medical aid to [[India]] as it deals with a surge in cases. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/04/25/us-pledges-medical-aid-for-india-to-combat-surge-484584 (''Politico'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Killing of Sarah Halimi]]
**Thousands of people march in protest in [[Paris]] and several other cities around the world after the French [[Court of Cassation (France)|Court of Cassation]] announces that the accused [[murder (French law)|murder]]er of Lucie Attal, also known as Sarah Halimi, would not be taken to trial, as they judged that the incident had occurred while the suspect was in the midst of a [[cannabis]]-induced "delusional fit", which therefore [[Bouffée délirante|rendered them not culpable]] in the killing. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/apr/25/protest-in-france-as-man-accused-of-killing-jewish-woman-avoids-trial (''The Guardian'')]
